item.title: The six rungs of being found: SEO, SMO, AEO, GEO, DEO and SXO
item.description: Six ways a customer finds you, trusts you and calls you in 2026: SEO, SMO, AEO, GEO, DEO and SXO, explained in plain words by an Adelaide developer.

item.title: SEO for small business in 2026: what still works
item.description: Plain-English SEO for a small Australian business in 2026: what Google still rewards, what AI Overviews changed, and the nine checks that matter most.

item.title: What is SMO? Social media optimisation for small business
item.description: SMO is making your pages look right and get found when they're shared. The tags, the 1200×630 card and the profile links that do it, with the checks.

item.title: What is AEO? Answer engine optimisation, in plain words

item.title: What is GEO? How to get your business cited by ChatGPT, Perplexity and Google's AI

item.title: What is DEO? Getting chosen after you've been found

item.title: What is SXO? Search experience optimisation explained

item.title: Three things shipped today
item.description: A seat-view demo with a QR code for walk-ins, a site that says what it is in plain words to people and AI search, and a board that now reaches the desk by itself.
item.content:encoded:
Three things shipped today.

The seat-view demo went live on blueprintau.com this morning. You pick a seat and see the view from it, and there's a QR code for walk-ins to scan at the counter.

Tonight the site learned to say what it is in plain words, to people and to AI search: who builds it, where, and what for. It also got a new preview card for when a link is shared. The first two uploads bounced because my home IP had fallen off the host's allowlist. Fixed, re-sent, live.

Then the desk. The Office bots keep their own board of 82 trade shops. Until now, getting it onto this desk meant a browser upload. Now the board goes straight to the server and the desk picks it up by itself. It has 101 tests, and all of them pass.

item.title: Week one: starting the diary
item.description: The first page of a working diary: five Glassbox releases, a playable ad that pours a beer, two tools for my own bench, the AI Answer Monitor, and a new site.
item.content:encoded:
This is the first page of a working diary. From here on it's one short entry a night: what got built, what shipped, what broke.

This week needs a catch-up, so here it is.

Glassbox had five releases between Tuesday and Thursday. It's my open-source tool for seeing what AI coding agents actually do. "collect" rolls every machine's report into one fleet view. "fence" finds secrets (keys, tokens, passwords) that ended up in session transcripts and can shred them in place. "adhere" reads a project's CLAUDE.md and checks, line by line, whether the agent followed it. Its first run scored the session that built it at 22%. Then 0.9.1 added a loop guard that stops an agent repeating a tool call that has already failed twice.

Pour is the second "ad for the ad". It's a 30-second playable: hold to pour a beer, let go at the line. Then it turns out to be an ad for BlueprintAU builds.

Two tools for my own bench. Aldo Motion is a motion-graphics editor that runs in the browser and exports MP4, GIF and live HTML. SFTP Deploy pushes a site to the host, shows what will change first, and backs up anything it overwrites.

The AI Answer Monitor is designed. It's the paid follow-on to the Six-Rung Check: every week it asks AI the ten questions a customer would ask about a trade in their area, then reports who got named.

And this site. aldo.today went from a domain sitting unused to live today: this diary out front, and a private desk behind it for the day's list, follow-ups and money.

Tomorrow's entry will be shorter.
